text: PolicyClaimsDB's schema has only ever existed as whatever state the live database happens to be in. This lesson puts it under source control, with a real deployment pipeline on top.

A Git-versioned SQL Server Database Project builds into a DACPAC on every pull request, runs a pre-deployment dry run, and only publishes for real once that dry run is reviewed and the change merges to main.
SqlPackage's Script action generates the exact T-SQL a deployment would run, without running it, so a reviewer can catch an unexpected DROP COLUMN before it ever touches production.
The real publish step runs only on merge, with BlockOnPossibleDataLoss as a backstop behind that human review -- it still stops a dangerous change even if a reviewer misses it.
Schema changes are now reviewed and automated like application code. Next: the first real test of the disaster-recovery setup built back in Lesson 11.
